note: Skeptic / future-maintainer angle. Only findings that survive the inclusion test keep severity; process-only nits are demoted. The reviser changelog is fifty-one identical “search/replace” lines and is treated as non-evidence of what actually changed.

findings.topic: closed NamedState enum vs coined surface states
findings.section: Binding definitions; W6; W14; W18; W19
findings.criterion: every surface works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero); no dead control
findings.message: W6 freezes a closed thirteen-member NamedState enum and a single render_state() primitive, and the binding text forbids waves from inventing trichotomy words. Later surface waves still invent user-facing states outside that set: W14 “named unavailable,” W18 “unsupported-preview,” W19 “unknown-preference.” A future maintainer must either (a) ship labels that bypass render_state (exactly the hand-invented labels the plan bans), or (b) silently overload unknown / cannot_* and collapse distinct failures. Either path re-creates dead or mislabelled empties on real controls. The enum, the binding allow-list, and every surface-local “named X state” must be one closed, amendable registry before surface waves run—not three competing vocabularies.

findings.section: Binding definitions (Vocabulary bijection); W8; Hardening-gate failure-state table vocabulary
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every health/usage/diagnose surface fails with a named, user-visible state
findings.message: The plan requires STATE-VOCABULARY-MAP.md to be a machine-read bijection where “every term on both sides appears exactly once,” then immediately violates that math: empty-but-valid splits into empty, zero_measured, and pending; cannot_* is an open family; surface tables must also carry separate unknown/empty rows in surface-native language. A future maintainer implementing table_validator.py cannot satisfy “exactly once both ways” and the multi-map / open-set rules at the same time. The validator will be weakened, skipped, or green while mapping wrong—and wrong maps are how unknown becomes empty and zero becomes subscription. Replace “bijection / exactly once” with an explicit multi-map schema (dependency term → one or more NamedState + required surface rows) and make that the only thing the validator enforces.

findings.section: W2 Exit register; uses of E1–E6 across W1, W4, W8, W12, W21, W22
findings.criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty / raw binary never exit via E6; nothing silent-claims the North Star
findings.message: W2 builds a machine exit register around ExitId E1–E6 and hard rules (E2 illegal for dollars, E6 closed for the four North-Star violation classes, no exit-justified-by-exit), but the draft never defines what E1, E3, E4, or E5 mean as exits—only scattered uses (“no E5 on the task triple,” E4 reduced instrumentation, E3 out-of-criteria, E1 not-available, E2 provisional-with-as_of). A future maintainer cannot implement validate_justification, conjunction scoring, or S1 routing without inventing semantics. Invented semantics are how a silent-zero or fabricated-dollar finding gets an illegal exit and how the terminal status string lies. Require a binding EXIT-SEMANTICS table (id, legal criteria, required evidence shape, forbidden justifications, user-visible substitute) as a W2 deliverable, and make every later E-reference a row id in that table.

findings.section: Success criteria; W2 terminal_status; W3 inventory scope; W21 TRACEABILITY-MATRIX
findings.criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor diagnose + session attach; every claiming surface honest; Steward proof only at S1
findings.message: The plan speaks of “ten criteria,” “criteria 1–8 plus open and run,” and a matrix with “one row per criterion 1–10,” but nowhere lists the numbered ten with stable names. Success criteria are a bullet soup; W3’s control list is partial; W21’s matrix cannot be filled without invention. A future maintainer (or Foreman wave) will invent criterion numbers, omit attach or restart, or stamp CANDIDATE-MET on the wrong row—then S1 cannot convert structure to MET honestly. Add a binding numbered criteria table (1–10, North-Star phrase, owning wave(s), inventory controls) and make terminal_status, freeze NORTH-STAR CONTROL DECISION, and TRACEABILITY-MATRIX import that table by id only.

findings.topic: containment path vs product write paths
findings.section: W1 containment smoke; Success criteria Handoff; product deliverables under anchor/, tools/, tests/
findings.criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators; open/run/stop/restart and Doctor/attach on branch v1.2 without dead controls
findings.message: W1 requires containment_smoke.py to assert “every write target resolves under planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/” while nearly every later wave’s real deliverables are product paths (anchor/ui/…, anchor/session/…, anchor/doctor/…, tools/, tests/). Handoff only clarifies that the doc-trio lives under planning/ and “root foreign Foreman artifacts” stay untouched—it does not reconcile the absolute “every write under planning/” rule with shipping v1.2 product code. A future maintainer will either (a) put production code under planning/ (unshippable to the real app), (b) write into Anchor and fail containment forever, or (c) disable the smoke and lose the v1.1.x safety floor. Split write classes in the smoke: planning artifacts must stay under stage2; product tree writes are allow-listed under explicit Anchor paths; foreign Foreman root artifacts remain byte-identical—and name the allow-list as a signed ledger row.

findings.section: Binding definitions; W8 table_validator; Hardening-gate Failure-state table vocabulary; wave-local failure-states/*.md
findings.criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero as separate user-visible states on every claiming surface
findings.message: Authors are told three incompatible table shapes at once: (1) five hardening dependency rows, (2) separate unknown and empty NamedState rows, (3) surface-native action language only, with index/rebuild banned on user tiles. W8 fails “honesty theater” and “missing required row,” but never shows one canonical filled table (columns, required keys, how empty-but-valid becomes two/three rows, where status code vs user text live). Future maintainers will copy the wrong shape; the validator will thrash; surfaces will green with merged unknown/empty. Ship one normative example table and a JSON/YAML schema the validator loads—prose checklists are not a schema.

findings.section: W10–W20 Depends-on graph; W21 surface-wave join gate
findings.criterion: open, run, stop, restart, Doctor diagnose, session attach all honest before North Star can be claimed
findings.message: Most Phase-3 waves declare Depends-on: W9 only; W11/W17 depend on W10 for dead_control; W21 depends only on W20 but then asserts a join gate over W10–W20 GREEN. Future maintainer / Foreman topo-sort can start W12–W20 before W10’s shared dead-control primitive exists, or treat W21 as unblocked when only W20 is green while restart or Doctor is still OPEN—exactly when a dead-control audit mistakes “not built yet” for “clean.” Encode the real DAG: shared primitives (W6–W10) before importers; W21 Depends-on: W10–W20 (or an explicit join wave), not W20 alone; ban parallel GO on importers until dead_control and render_state commit SHAs exist.

findings.section: plan header test-command; per-wave gate-command pytest
findings.criterion: surfaces work or fail named; cost never fabricates dollars (proof must be re-runnable)
findings.message: The Foreman-facing test-command is node scripts/run-all-tests.mjs, while every wave gate is scoped pytest -v on a dated file. The draft never defines what run-all-tests.mjs runs, whether it invokes the conformance harness / zero_inference_lint / table_validator, or which command is authoritative when they disagree. A future maintainer will green the wave pytest and leave the node suite broken (or the reverse), and regressions in dead controls or cost labelling will not be caught at the contract the orchestrator actually runs. Bind one composition rule: run-all-tests.mjs must invoke every wave gate-command plus conformance tools, or drop the node entry and make the pytest root the sole Foreman test-command.

findings.topic: plan-wide property gates without wave owners
findings.section: Property gates; Hardening-gate obligations; wave deliverables
findings.criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; remembered preference and live cadence must stay honest under re-entry
findings.message: The plan asserts honesty, idempotence, boundedness, and containment as plan-level properties, and says a named property without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER—yet only W1 (escape attempts), W3 (repeat-invocation), and a few numeric bounds are wave-owned. Preference persistence (W19), cadence (W20), inventory ledger writes, and cost migration claim durability-adjacent behaviour without atomic write/lock/concurrency obligations or per-wave idempotence tests. Future maintainers will treat the property-gate section as wallpaper; double-apply preference or cadence ticks will mislabel empty/unknown. Either attach each asserted property to concrete wave ids with named tests, or remove the plan-level assertion so the inclusion test does not lie.

findings.section: W4 rollup evidence / cost spot-check protocol
findings.message: Dollar honesty rests on a 0-cent independent spot-check and a rule that the aggregation author may not compute the second side. The draft never defines the machine record (fields for author identity, procedure path, session sample set, engine, both totals, disagreement) that the gate validates—only narrative rejection conditions. A future maintainer will store a checkbox “independent: true” and ship fabricated agreement. Specify the spot-check artifact schema, how author identity is host-attested (not agent-self-reported), and the exact gate failure strings when independence or sample floors fail—and refuse PROVEN cost without that artifact.

findings.section: Binding definitions (The state trichotomy); W6 NamedState
findings.message: Calling a four-word set a “trichotomy,” then adding a thirteen-state enum plus an allow-list of ok/unmeasured/measurement_failed/timeout/stale/cannot_*, guarantees vocabulary drift the next time someone “adds one more state.” Future maintainers will argue which set is canonical. Rename to “core four (empty / zero_measured / unknown / pending)” plus “extended NamedState registry,” and state that only the registry is renderable—no parallel “trichotomy” brand.

findings.topic: verbatim docstring lock on binding text
findings.section: W6 NamedState docstrings must match Binding definitions verbatim
findings.message: Coupling enum docstrings to the plan’s binding prose “verbatim” makes any clarity edit to the plan a red W6 gate. That is future-maintainer friction, not a North-Star honesty failure. Prefer a single imported constants module or hash of the binding fragment over full-prose equality—demote unless it causes label drift on screen.

Fifty-one identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines give a future shark or maintainer zero diff intent. Process defect for the planning loop, not a product North-Star violation—do not hold the wave list open on this alone, but stop accepting content-free changelogs.
